definition: A Mapping projects declared input values into a declared output shape. Its formal inputs are not storage records or domain edges.
inputs: Every v2 Mapping declares an ordered, dense inputs array of at most 128 unique name/type pairs, including an explicit empty array for a zero-argument Mapping. Legacy input is forbidden in v2; inputs is forbidden in v1.
calls: Arguments are type-checked by position and evaluated left to right exactly once before each Mapping evaluation. All formals are required, including nullable formals. Defaults use explicit coalesce expressions, not omitted arguments.
reuse: A value supplied as an argument may be used repeatedly without recomputation. Repeating a declared Calculation call expression evaluates it again. Zero-argument declarations retain invocation-local memoization; parameterized Mapping calls are not memoized.
trace: v2 Mapping trace carries ordered inputs and its evaluation policy. Existing composition maps-from/maps-to roles describe record input and output types; scalar inputs remain typed values, never invented ontology nodes. Explicit Calculation calls appear as composition calls, never new canonical domain relations.
compatibility: v1 source and trace generation are unchanged. Node and Rust lower the same v2 arguments; old AlchLang authoring and typed-mapping/v1 are not reinterpreted.
validation_ceiling: Existing declarative type and runtime perimeter only; no new runtime argument normalization, deep immutability, invariant execution, standalone bound Mapping profile, package qualification or authority claim.
